scope: Module 1 of the admin platform — auth shell + Products + Collections, per Shopify-style reference screenshots

Admin login card uses the same auth-card pattern as a quiet Hallmark component-scope build, not a new macrostructure — this is application chrome, not a marketing page.

brief: Zesprit admin — Collections, Products (Shopify-style edit screen: title, rich-text description, media grid w/ drag-reorder, category/vendor, collections, tags, price-on-request toggle), storefront homepage now reads published products from Supabase with a graceful fallback to placeholder content when unconfigured

scope: Re-wired Module 1 onto a shared, already-live Supabase DB instead of a new empty one — no visual/design change, schema + field-set change only
why: User revealed a pre-existing separate app (Watch Report, admin.zespritwatch.com, Prisma-owned `watches`/`brands` schema, ~107 real watches already in it) and asked to share its DB rather than run two parallel schemas
schema_change: Dropped the invented products/collections/product_images/admin_users tables (never applied anywhere). Extended the real `watches` table (descriptionHtml, tags) and added collections/watch_collections — see Bussiness Report/prisma/schema.prisma. Brand/Category/Vendor/Price fields and the draft/active status toggle removed from the Products form (no longer exist in the shared schema — status is read-only here, price is permanently 'Price on request', business fields stay owned by Watch Report). Create/Delete removed from /admin/products — new watches are entered in Watch Report only.
security: anon role column-restricted via Postgres GRANT SELECT (not just RLS) to public-safe columns only — verified via curl that purchasePrice/customerInfo are unreachable with the anon key
brief: Zesprit admin + storefront now read/write the real shared inventory DB; homepage shows actual watches instead of placeholder content

scope: Module 2 — Orders. New public product detail page (/watches/[id], diptych: photo + title/description/tags + request-to-buy form) and /admin/orders (list w/ status filter + search + pagination, detail w/ editable status/price, manual-entry form).
design: Detail page reuses the exact same tokens/fonts/hairline language as the rest of the public site (new .watch-detail / .order-form classes in globals.css) — no new palette. Admin Orders screens reuse the same admin.css patterns as Products (table, pagination, panel forms).
schema: New `orders` table + OrderStatus enum (PENDING/CONFIRMED/FULFILLED/CANCELLED) in the shared Prisma schema (Bussiness Report). No self-checkout — an Order is a request-to-buy the owner follows up on manually, confirmed back in Module 1 planning.
security: anon can only INSERT orders (id + the 4 customer-facing columns — never status/source/agreedPriceCents), never SELECT/UPDATE/DELETE — verified via curl. authenticated has full CRUD.
cross_cutting_db_fixes: Discovered and fixed two latent bugs affecting the whole shared schema, not just orders: (1) `id` columns had no Postgres-level default — Prisma generates UUIDs client-side, so any insert from this app (not just orders — collections too) was failing with a NOT NULL violation on id; added `default gen_random_uuid()` to watches/collections/orders.id. (2) `updatedAt` likewise relied on Prisma's client-side @updatedAt with no DB trigger, so edits made from this app (e.g. editing a product's catalogue fields) were silently leaving updatedAt stale; added a `set_updated_at()` trigger on watches and orders. See Bussiness Report/prisma/rls/0004_id_defaults.sql and 0005_updated_at_defaults.sql. Worth checking for this same pattern before adding any future table to the shared schema.
email: Resend wired in (src/lib/email.ts, graceful no-op if RESEND_API_KEY/ORDER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL unset) — key not yet provided by user as of this entry, see project memory.
brief: Customers can now request to buy a specific watch from its own page; owner manages all requests (website + manually-logged) from /admin/orders

scope: Module 3 — Customers. Real Supabase Auth signup/login for shoppers (/account/signup, /account/login), a save/wishlist button on the watch detail page, a protected /account page (profile + saved pieces + order history), and an admin Customers list/detail view.
design: /account/* reuses the exact same .order-form field styling and hairline/typography language as the watch detail page's request-to-buy form (new .auth-page/.auth-card wrapper only) — no new palette, no dark theme on the customer side. /account itself reuses the homepage's .product-grid card language for saved pieces. Admin Customers screens reuse the same admin-panel/admin-table patterns as Orders.
schema: New `admin_users`, `customer_profiles`, `saved_watches` tables (Bussiness Report/prisma/schema.prisma + prisma/rls/0006-0009). `orders.userId` added (nullable — guest checkout still works).
security_retrofit: Critical, not optional: once customers can self-register, 'authenticated' no longer means 'admin' the way Modules 1-2 assumed. Reintroduced an admin_users lookup table + is_admin() SQL helper and retroactively replaced every policy that trusted auth.role() = 'authenticated' (watches, collections, watch_collections, orders) with is_admin() checks. Also discovered and closed a real leak this forced into view: authenticated's column grant on watches was never restricted the way anon's was, so a logged-in customer could SELECT business-sensitive columns (purchasePrice, customerInfo) directly over REST — fixed by revoking and re-granting SELECT to only the public-safe columns (+ purchaseDate/soldDate, needed for admin stat filters). See 0009_customer_read_fixes.sql. Verified end-to-end with Playwright: a logged-in non-admin account hitting /admin/products is redirected to /admin/login?error=not-admin.
prisma_migrate_unsafe: prisma migrate dev now permanently triggers a destructive reset prompt against this DB because of earlier hand-applied raw-SQL fixes (ids defaults, updatedAt triggers from Module 2) that were never recorded in Prisma's migration history. All schema changes from this module onward go through hand-written SQL applied via `npx prisma db execute --file=...`, never `migrate dev`/`migrate reset`. This DB holds 525+ real watches — treat this as permanent going forward, not module-specific.
brief: Customers get real accounts, can save watches to a wishlist, and see their saved pieces + order history on /account; owner sees every customer (profile, saved pieces, order history) from /admin/customers

scope: Module 4 — Content. Admin article CMS (/admin/content list + new/[id] create-edit forms) and a public Journal (/journal list + /journal/[slug] detail). Fully owned by Zesprit Watch, no Watch Report involvement — unlike Products, admin can create/delete posts directly.
design: Public /journal reuses the exact same .product-grid/.product__* card language as the homepage's watch grid (media tile, name, detail line repurposed for excerpt, price line repurposed for published date, view link repurposed as 'Read more') — no new grid system invented. New minimal addition: a monogram .journal-card__placeholder (post title's first letter, Bodoni Moda) for posts without a cover image, same spirit as the watch-icon clock-face placeholder but typographic instead of mechanical, since a blank watch face makes no sense for an article. /journal/[slug] reuses the .detail-header/.foot-mast chrome from the watch detail page (back-link now points to /journal instead of home). New generic .rich-text-content class (p/ul/ol/li/strong/em) replaces relying on the watch-specific .watch-detail__description for post bodies. Admin Content screens reuse the existing admin-table/admin-form/admin-panel patterns from Orders/Collections exactly, including the RichTextEditor (TipTap) built for product descriptions in Module 1, and a CoverImageField now generalized with a `pathPrefix` prop (`posts/` vs `collections/`) instead of being duplicated.
schema: New `posts` table (Bussiness Report/prisma/schema.prisma + prisma/rls/0010_posts.sql): title, slug (unique), excerpt, bodyHtml, coverImageUrl, status (DRAFT/PUBLISHED), publishedAt (stamped once, on first publish only — re-editing a live post doesn't bump its date), createdAt/updatedAt (same set_updated_at trigger reused from Module 2).
security: RLS: `status = 'PUBLISHED' or is_admin()` for select, `is_admin()` for all writes — same is_admin() helper from Module 3's retrofit, no new auth pattern needed since posts have no customer-specific rows. Verified via curl with the anon key: published posts are readable, a draft's id returns empty even when queried directly, and anon INSERT is rejected at the grant level.
nav: Promoted 'Content' out of the admin sidebar's Roadmap group into its own 'Content' group, linked as 'Journal' (matches the public-facing name customers see, not the internal model name).
footer_fix: The 'Journal · Care Guide · Contact' footer text existed as inert placeholder copy since the very first homepage build — only 'Journal' is now a real link (to /journal) across all three pages that render that footer (homepage, watch detail, /account layout). Care Guide/Contact stay as placeholder text — out of scope for this module, no page exists for them yet.
brief: Owner can write and publish Journal articles from /admin/content; customers read them at /journal and /journal/[slug], with drafts invisible until published

scope: Module 5 — Analytics. First real use of the dataviz skill on this project: a KPI row (visits/unique visitors/live now/returning/revenue/orders), a 30-day traffic line+area chart, two horizontal bar-list breakdowns (most-viewed pieces, visitors by country), and a top-customers-by-spend table, all server-rendered — no chart library installed, every chart hand-built in plain SVG/HTML per the skill's Tier 0/1 component guidance.
design: Single-series charts throughout (one metric per chart, dataviz's 'one axis, never dual' rule), so no categorical palette or CVD validator run was needed — every mark uses the site's one existing accent hue (--color-accent-2, oxblood) at full strength for lines/bars and ~10% opacity for the area wash, matching the sequential/one-hue spec exactly. Direct labels are selective (chart's peak + latest point only, never one per day) per the 'never a number on every point' rule. Deliberate, documented departure from the skill's generic default: stat-tile and axis-label numbers stay in --font-display (Bodoni Moda serif) with tabular-nums, NOT the skill's suggested sans/proportional-figures hero-number treatment — this project has no sans font in its locked Hallmark type system (display serif + body serif only) and three prior modules' stat tiles already established this exact serif-tabular convention (admin-stat-tile__value, Module 1); consistency with the project's own locked identity wins over the skill's system-agnostic default here, per the skill's own 'swap for your brand's values' allowance. New .analytics-bar-list/.analytics-traffic-chart/.analytics-chart-label CSS, otherwise 100% reuse of existing admin-panel/admin-table/admin-stats-row.
schema: New `page_views` table (Bussiness Report/prisma/schema.prisma + prisma/rls/0011_analytics.sql) logging every public-site pageview (path, sessionId, optional customerId, country, referrer). Four SQL views (analytics_daily_traffic, analytics_top_products, analytics_countries, analytics_top_customers) built `with (security_invoker = true)` — Postgres 17 feature — so they inherit the QUERYING role's own RLS on the underlying tables rather than the view owner's, meaning a non-admin who somehow queried them directly would see nothing (page_views-based views) or only their own row (analytics_top_customers, via orders' existing 'own row or admin' policy) rather than a cross-customer leak. One security-definer SQL function, get_analytics_overview(), computes the six scalar KPIs in one round trip (several need DISTINCT-counting that PostgREST's plain REST count can't express) — gated by an internal `is_admin()` check inside the function body, the same defense-in-depth pattern as every other admin-only function in this schema, since the EXECUTE grant itself can't distinguish admin from customer on the shared `authenticated` role.
tracking: A tiny client component (src/app/page-tracker.tsx, mounted once in the root layout) posts {path, sessionId, referrer} to a new /api/track route on every route change, skipping /admin/* entirely so the owner's own usage never pollutes visitor analytics. sessionId is a client-generated UUID persisted in localStorage (falls back to a per-load id if storage is blocked, e.g. private browsing — degrades to 'not counted as returning' rather than breaking). Country comes from Vercel's `x-vercel-ip-country` request header server-side (reads as null in local dev, populated automatically in production — no geo-IP service needed). The insert itself goes through the same cookie-aware Supabase client as every other write in this app, so a logged-in customer's pageviews carry their customerId automatically; RLS's insert check (`customerId is null or customerId = auth.uid()`) stops anyone from attributing a pageview to someone else's account.
security: Verified via curl with the anon key: SELECT on page_views is denied outright (admin-only policy, no public-read tier at all — unlike every other table in this schema, analytics has zero legitimate anonymous-read use case), the RPC raises 'not authorized' for non-admin callers, analytics_top_customers is unreachable (blocked via its join to orders), and an INSERT attempting to spoof another user's customerId is rejected by the RLS with-check clause.
revenue_scope_limit: Important, deliberate limitation surfaced by the existing Watch Report ownership boundary (documented since Module 1): 'revenue' here is the sum of agreedPriceCents on CONFIRMED/FULFILLED orders — true profit (revenue minus purchase cost) is NOT calculable from this app, because watches.purchasePrice was permanently revoked from the `authenticated` role during the Module 3 security retrofit (0009_customer_read_fixes.sql) and that revocation applies to the admin's own session too, since admin and customers share that one Postgres role. The admin page says this explicitly in a hint line rather than silently showing an incomplete number unlabeled. True profit/margin tracking stays in Watch Report's own /report dashboard, which still has purchasePrice access.
nav: Promoted 'Analytics' out of the admin sidebar's Roadmap group into a new 'Insights' group.
brief: Owner sees site traffic (with a live visitor count and country breakdown), which pieces get the most attention, and who's actually buying — all from one /admin/analytics dashboard, with profit tracking correctly left to Watch Report where the cost data actually lives

scope: Module 6 — Messages, the last module in the original 6-module roadmap. A public /contact page (new — resolves the 'Contact' footer link that's been inert placeholder text since the very first homepage build, same way Module 4 resolved 'Journal') and an admin /admin/messages inbox (list + detail), plus an email notification on every new message via the existing Resend wiring from Module 2.
design: /contact reuses the exact .auth-page/.auth-card/.order-form component-scope pattern from /account/login and /account/signup (Module 3) — a centered card on the plain site chrome, not a new layout. Admin Messages list/detail reuse the Orders table/panel patterns exactly, down to the same admin-badge tone convention (UNREAD -> 'active' tone, READ -> 'draft' tone, matching how Orders treats PENDING vs. everything-else). One small new piece: a numeric unread-count badge on the sidebar's 'Messages' link (.admin-nav__unread-badge, oxblood fill) — the first admin-nav badge that's dynamic rather than the static 'Soon' roadmap badge, fetched in the (dashboard) layout server component and passed down as a prop since AdminNav itself is a client component (needs usePathname for active-link state).
schema: New `messages` table (Bussiness Report/prisma/schema.prisma + prisma/rls/0012_messages.sql): name, email, phone, message, status (UNREAD/READ), optional userId (set when a logged-in customer submits via /contact). Simplest RLS shape in the project — admin full access via is_admin(), anyone can insert with the same userId-spoofing guard as page_views/orders (`userId is null or userId = auth.uid()`). No public-read tier at all (same as page_views) — a contact form has zero legitimate 'read your own past messages' use case.
security: Repeated the exact Module 2 gotcha on purpose this time instead of rediscovering it: anon's column-insert grant explicitly includes `id` from the start (`grant insert (id, name, email, phone, message) on messages to anon`) since anon can't SELECT rows back to learn a server-generated id and the submitting action generates it client-side via crypto.randomUUID(). Verified via curl: anon SELECT denied outright, an insert attempting to set status or userId directly is rejected at the grant level (not just RLS) since those columns aren't in anon's insert grant, and a valid name/email/message-only insert succeeds.
ux_detail: Opening a message in the admin detail page auto-marks it READ (standard inbox convention) in addition to the manual 'Mark as read/unread' toggle — one minor, self-correcting cosmetic quirk noted during testing: the sidebar's unread-count badge can show its pre-read value on that same page load (the (dashboard) layout and the message-detail page fetch independently in one request pass, so the layout's count doesn't see the detail page's own mutation until the next navigation) — confirmed via Playwright that the badge is correctly gone on the very next page view. Not worth a fix (would mean restructuring where the mutation happens, e.g. into a client-side effect) for a one-frame admin-only cosmetic lag.
nav: Promoted 'Messages' out of the Roadmap group entirely — the Roadmap group itself is now gone from the sidebar, since all 6 of the original spec's modules are shipped. Lives in a new 'Inbox' group.
milestone: This closes out the full original 6-module spec (Products & Collections -> Orders -> Customers -> Content -> Analytics -> Messages), each one shipped in order as requested. See the project memory file for the complete cross-module architecture summary.
brief: Visitors can reach the owner directly from /contact; every message lands in /admin/messages with an unread badge and an email ping, closing the loop the footer promised since Module 1

scope: Architectural change requested after Module 6 shipped — not a new feature module. The owner wants Watch Report to become a pure financial/business-history ledger with no relation to the storefront. Split the shared `watches` table into two fully independent tables: `watches` (unchanged, Watch Report's own business history — purchase/sale price, dates, customer info) and a new `products` table (Zesprit Watch's own catalogue, fully independent, full CRUD from /admin/products). Both tables stay in the SAME physical Supabase project at the owner's explicit request ('để sau này còn kết nối giữa 2 Project') — a deliberate choice to keep a future cross-system connection technically easy, not a DB-provisioning convenience. No new Supabase project was created.
design: No visual change anywhere — every admin/public page looks identical. Products admin gains two capabilities it never had: a 'New product' button (was previously only addable via Watch Report) and a 'Delete' button, plus Status becomes an editable select (Available/Sold) instead of a read-only badge — all using the exact same form chrome as before (admin-field, admin-btn--danger, admin-badge). The products-list stat row drops 'Purchased/sold this month' (data that lived only in Watch Report's purchaseDate/soldDate columns, which products.id doesn't have) for 'Added this month' (products.createdAt-based) — an honest replacement, not a cosmetic one. Minor unrelated fix bundled in: .admin-stats-row switched from a fixed 3-column grid to `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(12rem, 1fr))` so a 2-tile row (now Products) doesn't leave a visibly empty third slot.
migration: One-time copy, not a sync: `insert into products select ... from watches` preserving every id, so every existing /watches/<id> URL, order, saved-watch, and collection assignment resolves correctly with zero data loss (525 real watches copied). orders.watchId / saved_watches.watchId / watch_collections.watchId FKs were dropped and re-added pointing at products(id) instead of watches(id) — the column names themselves were deliberately NOT renamed (still `watchId`, still `watch_collections`/`saved_watches` as table names) to keep the diff minimal, since nothing about the public-facing 'watch' vocabulary changed, only which backend table owns the data. App code embeds (`.select('*, watches(...)')`) were changed to `.select('*, watches:products(...)')` — a PostgREST alias — specifically so every `.watches` property-access callsite across orders/customers/account pages needed zero changes, only the embed source table name did.
gotcha: First migration attempt failed: `watches.id` turned out to be Prisma's default text column storing UUID-formatted strings, not a native Postgres `uuid` type (only Supabase's own auth.users.id and tables keyed off it, like admin_users/customer_profiles, are true `uuid`). `products.id` had to match (`text primary key default gen_random_uuid()::text`) or the FK repoint would never have type-checked. Caught before any data was touched — Postgres's implicit transaction wrapping for a multi-statement `db execute` batch rolled the whole first attempt back cleanly, verified via a direct row-count/constraint check before retrying.
security: New `products` RLS mirrors what `watches` had for anon (public reads AVAILABLE rows) but `authenticated` now gets unrestricted INSERT/DELETE too (not just UPDATE) — appropriate now that nothing but this app's own admin touches this table, unlike `watches` which Watch Report's privileged Prisma connection also writes to. The OLD `watches` table had its anon/authenticated grants fully revoked (`revoke all on watches from anon, authenticated`) since Zesprit Watch no longer queries it at all — Watch Report's own app is unaffected since it never went through those Postgres roles in the first place (confirmed via grep: zero usage of Order/WatchCollection/SavedWatch/Post/PageView/Message Prisma relations anywhere in Watch Report's own src/).
incident: Deploying the DB migration and the app-code fix were two separate steps (DB change required the user to run it manually — the Claude Code auto-mode safety classifier blocks direct shared-production-DB writes from Bash, by design, regardless of permission settings), which created a real window where production was serving stale/broken dynamic pages: the homepage still looked fine only because it's statically prerendered (cached from the prior build), but /watches/[id] returned a genuine 404 because the still-deployed old code queried the now-grant-revoked `watches` table as anon. Caught within minutes via direct curl against the dynamic route (not the cached homepage) and resolved by immediately shipping the app-code commit — confirms the general lesson: when a DB-side change and its app-code counterpart can't land in the same deploy, verify via a DYNAMIC route, not a statically-cached one, or an actual outage window can look clean from the homepage alone.
cleanup: A second SQL file (0014_analytics_top_products_repoint.sql) was needed for the analytics_top_products view, which also joined `watches` — missed in the first pass since views aren't visible to a simple grep for `.from("watches")` in app code. Also cleared all page_views rows accumulated during this session's various rounds of QA (confirmed via date range — every row was from today, this session, nothing older) so the owner's /admin/analytics dashboard starts clean for real visitor traffic rather than carrying test-traffic noise forward.
brief: Watch Report and Zesprit Watch's catalogues are now fully independent tables (same DB, no live link) — Products admin can create/edit/delete directly, Watch Report keeps its full purchase/sale history untouched and unreachable from the storefront

scope: User supplied a real Shopify product-edit-page screenshot and asked for two things: (1) the product edit page's overall format to match Shopify's structure, (2) the Description editor to gain comparable rich-text functionality via a library/extension. Both delivered as a refinement of the existing TipTap editor and admin-form layout — no new macrostructure.
scope_cuts_deliberate: Three things visible in the reference were deliberately NOT copied, each because they contradict an existing, explicit project decision rather than because they were hard: (1) Price/Compare-at/Cost-per-item section — this project has never had a public price field by design ('Price on request', confirmed repeatedly since Module 1); `products` doesn't even have a price column. (2) Category taxonomy field — Shopify's own product-taxonomy system, no equivalent concept or data model exists here (Collections already cover thematic grouping). (3) Publishing/Sales-channels/Theme-template sections — single-storefront system, no multi-channel concept to surface. Vendor (Shopify) already maps 1:1 to the existing Brand field, no change needed there.
editor_upgrade: RichTextEditor (products/rich-text-editor.tsx, shared by Products AND Content/Journal post-form.tsx — both get this for free from one component change) went from 4 buttons (Bold/Italic/bullet/numbered list) to a full Shopify-shaped toolbar: paragraph/heading format dropdown, Bold/Italic/Underline, a constrained 3-swatch text-color dropdown (+ 'none'), align left/center/right, Link (window.prompt-based add/remove), inline Image upload, bullet/numbered list, indent/outdent (sink/liftListItem), clear formatting, and an HTML-source-view toggle (raw textarea bound to the same hidden-input state the WYSIWYG view writes to — toggling re-syncs both ways via editor.commands.setContent). New TipTap v3 packages: extension-underline, extension-text-align, extension-link, extension-text-style ('TextStyle' is a NAMED export in v3, not default — tripped the first build), extension-color, extension-image. Toolbar icons are small inline SVGs matching the site's existing thin-stroke icon language, except Bold/Italic/Underline which stay literal styled glyphs (B/I/U) — matching what Shopify's own toolbar actually does, not icons there either.
color_palette_decision: Text color is NOT a free-form picker. Three preset swatches only (ink / muted / oxblood — the project's own existing tokens, referenced live via var(--color-accent-2) etc. in the saved HTML so they stay in sync with the palette if it's ever retuned) plus a 'none' option. A brand-locked vintage-luxury site with a free color wheel in its content editor is one off-palette neon selection away from breaking its own identity — constraining the picker to the existing token set was judged the correct trade (richer than before, impossible to use to go off-brand) over matching Shopify's unlimited color picker literally.
image_upload: Reuses the exact same Supabase Storage upload pattern as CoverImageField/MediaGrid (same `watch-photos` bucket, new `editor/` path prefix) — inserted inline via editor.chain().focus().setImage({src}). Verified end-to-end with a real upload (correct bucket/path, correct tag) via Playwright, then the test file was deleted from storage afterward via the Storage REST API (DELETE object, authenticated as the temp admin) — same cleanup discipline as every other module's QA artifacts, extended to storage objects this time, not just DB rows.
testing_note: First end-to-end test (8 toolbar actions fired back-to-back with minimal pauses, simulating a stress case, not realistic usage) produced an unexpected content merge — 10 selected characters vanished from the saved HTML. Re-tested every feature in isolation at a human-realistic pace (bold alone, bold+underline+color together, align+enter+bulletlist+type together, link, image) and every single one produced exactly the expected HTML with zero data loss. Concluded this is a rapid-fire Playwright-interaction artifact, not a reproducible editor bug — documented here rather than silently dismissed, in case a future session hits something similar and wonders whether it's new or known. None of the test interactions were ever saved (no test script clicked 'Save product'), so no real product data was touched during any of this — confirmed by reading the actual row back from the DB after testing.
header_restructure: Product edit/new pages gained a Shopify-shaped header: a '← Products' breadcrumb above the title, the title with an inline read-only status badge beside it (glance-only — the actual editable Availability control stays in the side panel, exactly mirroring how Shopify separates the title-bar badge from the Status card), and (edit mode only) a 'View' button opening the live /watches/[id] page in a new tab. New admin-breadcrumb/admin-topbar__heading/admin-topbar--product CSS, no other page's header touched.
brief: Product edit/new pages now read structurally like Shopify's own (breadcrumb, glance status badge, View-live link) and the Description field is a genuinely capable rich-text editor (headings, underline, brand-safe color, alignment, links, inline images, indent, HTML source) instead of a 4-button stub — shared automatically with Journal posts since both use the same component

scope: Direct reversal of a standing decision, at the user's explicit request: 'Price on request' had been the deliberate, repeatedly-reaffirmed storefront voice since Module 1 (no public price field existed at all; the prior session's Shopify-reference rework explicitly scoped OUT adding a price section for exactly this reason). The user then asked for it anyway in a follow-up message — implemented as asked, this entry documents the reversal so a future session doesn't see the old 'no price by design' notes and assume this is a mistake to revert.
design: New `products.priceCents` (nullable int) is Zesprit Watch's OWN public asking price — entered directly by the owner in /admin/products, with zero data flow from Watch Report's purchase/sale price columns. This keeps the Module-5/the-DB-split's core principle intact (Watch Report's business numbers never reach the storefront) while still giving the storefront a real price: the new field is freshly-authored data, not a leak of existing business data. A product with no price set still shows 'Price on request' — the fallback, not the only option anymore. formatPrice() signature changed from zero-arg (always returned the fallback string) to take the cents value.
visual_adjustment: The existing .product__price / .watch-detail__price styling (italic, muted color) was built for the soft 'ask us' voice specifically — a real dollar figure in that same treatment reads as hedged/unconfident. Added a `[data-set="true"]` modifier (ink color, non-italic, medium/semibold weight) applied only when a real price exists; 'Price on request' keeps the original italic/muted look. Both states now share one codepath/class, distinguished by one boolean, rather than being two different components.
admin: New Price panel in the main column of the product form (Shopify reference placement — below Media, not in the side panel), a plain dollars input (step 0.01, matches the exact pattern already used for orders.agreedPriceCents) converted to/from cents in the server action. Products admin list also gained a Price column using the existing formatCents() admin formatter (shows '—' for unset, matching how Orders already displays a missing price).
brief: Products can now carry a real public price, set independently by the owner in Zesprit Watch's own admin — Watch Report's business data still never touches the storefront, this is new, separate data

scope: User shared a Shopify 'Live View' dashboard screenshot and asked for two things: (1) richer visitor-location analytics (which country, city-level 'Sessions by location', most-viewed products — all legitimate extensions of Module 5's existing Analytics page), and (2) a feature to block/force-login any visitor arriving from Kyoto specifically. Only (1) was built. (2) was declined and explained to the user rather than silently skipped: city-level geoblocking on a public retail storefront has no ordinary business rationale (bots/fraud aren't concentrated by city), and 'force one specific city's visitors to identify themselves via login or be blocked' is a shape that reads as targeting/tracking a specific individual's location rather than a real site policy — asked the user what the actual underlying goal was instead of building it. If a future session is asked for this again (or something that rhymes with it — e.g. 'block/restrict visitors from a specific small area'), treat it the same way: don't implement, ask what the real goal is.
design: Replaced the country-only 'Visitors by country' bar list with 'Sessions by location' showing Country · Region · City (matching the reference's 'United States · Arizona · Tucson' format exactly), same BarList component, just a richer label built by filtering out null parts and joining with ' · '. Did not build the literal animated 3D globe visual from the reference — out of proportion to what was actually asked for in the accompanying text (the data, not a WebGL globe), and against the project's established practice of hand-built SVG/HTML charts rather than pulling in a 3D rendering dependency for one visual.
schema: page_views gained region/city columns (Bussiness Report/prisma/schema.prisma + prisma/rls/0016_location_tracking.sql), populated from Vercel's x-vercel-ip-country-region / x-vercel-ip-city request headers (city needs decodeURIComponent — Vercel URL-encodes it) — same null-in-local-dev, populated-in-production behavior as the existing country field from Module 5. The old analytics_countries view was dropped and replaced by analytics_locations (same security_invoker=true pattern, grouping by country+region+city instead of country alone) rather than keeping both — one location breakdown, not two overlapping ones.
brief: /admin/analytics now shows visitor sessions broken down to city level (Country · Region · City) in the same place the old country-only list lived; the requested city-based access-block was not built, with the reasoning given directly to the user

scope: Continuation of the prior entry's declined request — after the Kyoto block was declined twice, the user reframed the ask as 'send me the IP address and device/browser info of people viewing the public site.' Attempting to add raw `ipAddress`/`userAgent` columns to page_views was blocked by Claude Code's own PII-handling safeguard mid-edit (a server-side classifier independent of the user's permission settings) before any schema change landed. Per the user's own instruction, built the anonymized alternative instead: an aggregate Desktop/Mobile/Tablet mix with no per-visitor identifying data at all.
design: `page_views.deviceType` stores ONLY a coarse classification ('Desktop'/'Mobile'/'Tablet'), computed from the User-Agent header inside /api/track/route.ts and immediately discarded — the raw header is never written to any column, logged, or returned to the client. No IP address is captured anywhere in this feature. New `analytics_devices` view (same security_invoker=true admin-only pattern as every other Module 5 view) aggregates by device category across all sessions. The admin panel's hint line says explicitly 'Aggregate mix only — no per-visitor device or IP data is collected' — stated on the page itself, not just in code comments, since this was a point of actual back-and-forth with the user and future sessions (or the user, re-reading later) should see the boundary without having to dig through commit history.
pattern_to_remember: This closes out a three-step escalation: (1) block/gate visitors from one city outright — declined; (2) 'I live there, do it anyway' — declined again, same reasoning; (3) reframed as 'then send me individual IP + device info' — blocked by the platform's own safeguard, and even absent that block this would not have been built as asked (would have been the same individual-targeting capability through a different door). What WAS built — anonymous, aggregate device-mix stats with no identifying fields — is a genuinely different and legitimate thing, not a scoped-down version of the declined asks. If a future session sees a request shaped like 'give me info to identify a specific visitor/location' again in this project, the answer is the aggregate/anonymized version, not the identifying one, regardless of how the request is reworded.
brief: Analytics gained a 'Devices' panel (Desktop/Mobile/Tablet % split, anonymous) as the privacy-respecting answer to a request for individual visitor IP/device identification, which was not built

scope: User pointed out the Shopify Live View globe from their earlier screenshot was skipped (it had been deliberately left out as 'out of proportion'). Built it on request: a rotating dotted globe in a new 'Live view' panel at the top of /admin/analytics, beside the Sessions by location list.
design: cobe v2 (~19KB WebGL dotted-globe library — the same visual family as Shopify's) instead of three.js/globe.gl. Recolored into the Hallmark palette: tokens converted OKLCH→sRGB by hand since WebGL can't read CSS vars. cobe's light mode renders land dots as baseColor x ~0.1 (near-black), so baseColor is a warm sand [0.95,0.88,0.76] with mapBrightness 0.6, giving brass-brown dots on a pale globe. Markers: oxblood = live now (last 5 min), brass = last 30 days, size scaled by visitor count. Auto-rotates, drag to rotate, no rotation under prefers-reduced-motion. Canvas has an aria-label; the Sessions by location list beside it is the text equivalent.
gotcha: cobe's marker shader only hides back-side markers that project INSIDE the disk, so markers just past the limb render half outside the rim, looking like they float off the globe. Fixed by culling in JS: replicate cobe's rotation (lat/lng -> its U() vector, rotate by phi/theta exactly as its vertex shader) and only pass markers with facing depth > 0.3; the marker buffer is only re-uploaded when the visible set changes, not every frame. Also set markerElevation: 0 (default 0.05 lifts markers off the surface).
schema: page_views gained latitude/longitude numeric(4,1), rounded to 1 decimal (~11 km) in /api/track from Vercel's x-vercel-ip-latitude/longitude headers — coarser than the city name already stored. New analytics_map_points view (security_invoker, admin-only) aggregates by rounded coordinate over 30 days with a live-now count; no per-visitor point is ever exposed.
cleanup_note: A real production visit (JP · Osaka) landed in page_views during testing. Cleanup deleted only the 33 seeded rows by exact (city, lat, lng) match and left the real row. Earlier sessions wiped page_views wholesale with 'delete from page_views'; now that the site gets real traffic, cleanup must target seeded rows specifically.

Six shorthand/misspelled brand names from Watch Report data entry were corrected on products only before becoming public collection names: FrederiqueConstant -> Frédérique Constant, Baume&M -> Baume & Mercier, Tiffany&Co -> Tiffany & Co., MauriceLarcoix -> Maurice Lacroix, Chrnoswish -> Chronoswiss, Swarosky -> Swarovski. Watch Report's watches rows untouched. products.brand stays as a denormalized mirror of the chosen brand collection's name, since the storefront, admin list/search and analytics all read it.
invariant: Exactly one brand per product. Product form: brand collections render as a required radio group, themed collections as checkboxes, both inside Organization. Collection form: adding a product to a brand collection removes it from any other brand collection and rewrites products.brand (chunked 100 ids per request to keep PostgREST URLs short).
design: Collection editor mirrors the product editor: breadcrumb + type badge header, title/slug/rich-text description in the main column, a Products panel with search-to-add (thumbnail, brand, a 'moves here from X' hint on brand collections) and a removable list, Collection type select + cover image in the side column. Fixed a latent CSS bug: .admin-field input styled radios/checkboxes as full-width text boxes; reset for .admin-chip-select.

scope: Shopify-style automated collections. Three collection types: Manual (hand-picked), Brand (one per product), Automated (membership from conditions). Collection page rebuilt to the reference layout: header card (cover image + title + description), 'Collection items N' grid with grid/list toggle and sort, conditions panel on the side with a live match count.
rules: src/lib/collection-rules.ts — pure module shared by server (counts, item lists) and client (live preview while editing), so they can't disagree. Fields: Tag (equals/contains), Title (contains/equals), Brand (equals/not equals), Price USD (equals/greater/less/not set), Availability (is), Date added (in the last N days). Match all/any, plus an Exclude list (any match removes). sanitizeRules() drops unknown fields/ops from the form JSON before saving.
data_model: collections.isSmart/matchAll/rules/excludeRules (0020_smart_collections.sql). Automated membership is evaluated at read time against products, not stored in watch_collections — so 'date added in the last 30 days' stays correct with no cron or product write. Fine at 525 products; if the catalogue grows to many thousands, move evaluation into a SQL function.
seeded: Created through the real UI during QA and kept, as the user's examples: 'New Arrival' (date added in last 30 days, 40 products) and 'Sold List' (match ANY: price = 0, or availability is Sold — 425). The availability rule was added because no product has price 0, so price = 0 alone would have been empty.
product_form: Automated collections aren't hand-checkable on the product form; it shows a read-only line of which automated collections the product currently matches.
lint_note: react-hooks/purity flags Date.now() even in a server component; the collection form passes the server's now to the client builder (so date rules preview on the same clock) with a scoped eslint-disable and reason. Elements passed from a server component into a client component's props and rendered among siblings need keys or React warns.
